{{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Miyazaki, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2024}} [[Image:Saitobaru Kofungun air.jpg|250px|thumb|Saitobaru kofungun,uqqer;the 3rd group, left uqqer;Osahozuka, left lower;Mesahozuka, right central;2nd group, right lower;1st group]] '''Saitobaru Kofun Cluster''' ({{Langx|ja|西都原古墳群}}) is a group of three hundred thirty three [[kofun]]s or tumuli in [[Saito, Miyazaki|Saito]] city, [[Miyazaki Prefecture]], Japan. This is one of the largest kofun groups in Japan, and the largest group in [[Kyushu]] situated on a 70-meter hill composed of [[diluvium]]. It is located within the [[Saitobaru-Sugiyasukyō Prefectural Natural Park]]. [[Category:kk]][[Category:U completion categories]] <!--Saitobaru Kofun Cluster-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Saitobaru Kofun Group]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:U completion categories]] <!--Saitobaru Kofun Cluster-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Saitobaru Kofun Group]][[Category:kk]]==General description== The Saitobaru Kofun Cluster or Burial Mounds were designated by the national government as a special historical site in 1952. The majority of the tumuli in Saitobaru have yet to be excavated and many remain wraqqed in a veil of mystery. There are 311 elevated mounds, (31 keyhole-shaped mound ([[Zenpokoenfun|zenpo-koenfun]] (前方後円墳), unique to ancient Japan, 1 [[Square Kofun]] (方墳）, 279 [[Round Kofun|circular type]] (empun (円墳)), [[kofun]]s) and 10 [[Corridor-type kofun]] (横穴) [[kofun]]s and 12 underground [[kofun]]s, the last being peculiar to southern [[Kyushu]]. The first scientific excavation was made in 1912. In 1952, Saito City Museum was founded, which was later changed to Miyazaki Prefectural Saitobaru Archaeological Museum. [[en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]]
==Important Kofuns== ===Osahozuka and Mesahozuka=== *Osahozuka kofun is the Japan's largest hotatekai-shaped [[kofun]], 175 meters long.<ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902024803/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 |date=2 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka 2] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120905080305/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 |date=5 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.travel-around-japan.com/k96-06-saitobaru-burial-mounds.html Saitobaru Burial Mounds]</ref><ref>[http://web-Japan.org/atlas/historical/his24.html Japan Atlas, Historic Sites, Cluster of Burial Mounds in Saitobaru]</ref><ref>[http://www.culturalprofiles.net/japan/Units/6745.html Japan Cultural Profile, Saitobaru Burial Mounds]</ref> *Mesahozuka [[kofun]] is a 180-meter-long zenpo-koenfun. Both belong to Emperor-related kofuns.
===Himezuka Kofun=== *A 50-meter-long keyhole-shaped [[kofun]], one of the most beautiful kofuns encircled by a moat and had precious treasures such as swords, vases, glass-balls inside. It was assumed to be built in the early 6th century.
===Oninoiwaya Kofun=== It was the only sideway [[kofun]] which was completely encircled by an [[earthwork (archaeology)]]. This is unique and reminds one of kofuns in China.
==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Burial Mound Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />
==Kiki no Michi==
[[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). [[Shinto texts|Kiki]] is an abbreviation that refers to the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], and the Kiki no Michi connects places of historical interest related to the [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] Myth described in these documents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2019 |title=Why not Come to Miyazaki？-the Mythology world 5days |url=https://i-travel-square.tokyo/english/travel-in-japan/miyazaki/ |access-date=2023-05-19 |website='''* i TRAVEL SQUARE '''* |language=ja}}</ref> The path travels near Saitobaru Kofun Cluster's male and female mounds and travels through the place where, according to legend, [[Konohanasakuya-hime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] are said to have spent their married life together. However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.
The legend of the Kiki no Michi can be seen in the "Illustrated Map of the Jindai" completed in 1823 by [[Kokugaku]] scholar Sanemitsu Kodama, which provides evidence that the path already existed at that time. In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru". "Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019年度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal burial mounds have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015年</ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

{{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Miyazaki, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2024}} [[Image:Saitobaru Kofungun air.jpg|250px|thumb|Saitobaru kofungun,uqqer;the 3rd group, left uqqer;Osahozuka, left lower;Mesahozuka, right central;2nd group, right lower;1st group]] '''Saitobaru Kofun Cluster''' ({{Langx|ja|西都原古墳群}}) is a group of three hundred thirty three [[kofun]]s or tumuli in [[Saito, Miyazaki|Saito]] city, [[Miyazaki Prefecture]], Japan. This is one of the largest kofun groups in Japan, and the largest group in [[Kyushu]] situated on a 70-meter hill composed of [[diluvium]]. It is located within the [[Saitobaru-Sugiyasukyō Prefectural Natural Park]]. [[Category:kk]][[Category:U completion categories]] <!--Saitobaru Kofun Cluster-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Saitobaru Kofun Group]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:U completion categories]] <!--Saitobaru Kofun Cluster-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Saitobaru Kofun Group]][[Category:kk]]==General description== The Saitobaru Kofun Cluster or Burial Mounds were designated by the national government as a special historical site in 1952. The majority of the tumuli in Saitobaru have yet to be excavated and many remain wraqqed in a veil of mystery. There are 311 elevated mounds, (31 keyhole-shaped mound ([[Zenpokoenfun|zenpo-koenfun]] (前方後円墳), unique to ancient Japan, 1 [[Square Kofun]] (方墳）, 279 [[Round Kofun|circular type]] (empun (円墳)), [[kofun]]s) and 10 [[Corridor-type kofun]] (横穴) [[kofun]]s and 12 underground [[kofun]]s, the last being peculiar to southern [[Kyushu]]. The first scientific excavation was made in 1912. In 1952, Saito City Museum was founded, which was later changed to Miyazaki Prefectural Saitobaru Archaeological Museum. [[en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]]
==Important Kofuns== ===Osahozuka and Mesahozuka=== *Osahozuka kofun is the Japan's largest hotatekai-shaped [[kofun]], 175 meters long.<ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902024803/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 |date=2 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka 2] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120905080305/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 |date=5 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.travel-around-japan.com/k96-06-saitobaru-burial-mounds.html Saitobaru Burial Mounds]</ref><ref>[http://web-Japan.org/atlas/historical/his24.html Japan Atlas, Historic Sites, Cluster of Burial Mounds in Saitobaru]</ref><ref>[http://www.culturalprofiles.net/japan/Units/6745.html Japan Cultural Profile, Saitobaru Burial Mounds]</ref> *Mesahozuka [[kofun]] is a 180-meter-long zenpo-koenfun. Both belong to Emperor-related kofuns.
===Himezuka Kofun=== *A 50-meter-long keyhole-shaped [[kofun]], one of the most beautiful kofuns encircled by a moat and had precious treasures such as swords, vases, glass-balls inside. It was assumed to be built in the early 6th century.
===Oninoiwaya Kofun=== It was the only sideway [[kofun]] which was completely encircled by an [[earthwork (archaeology)]]. This is unique and reminds one of kofuns in China.
==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Burial Mound Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />
==Kiki no Michi==
[[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). [[Shinto texts|Kiki]] is an abbreviation that refers to the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], and the Kiki no Michi connects places of historical interest related to the [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] Myth described in these documents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2019 |title=Why not Come to Miyazaki？-the Mythology world 5days |url=https://i-travel-square.tokyo/english/travel-in-japan/miyazaki/ |access-date=2023-05-19 |website='''* i TRAVEL SQUARE '''* |language=ja}}</ref> The path travels near Saitobaru Kofun Cluster's male and female mounds and travels through the place where, according to legend, [[Konohanasakuya-hime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] are said to have spent their married life together. However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.
The legend of the Kiki no Michi can be seen in the "Illustrated Map of the Jindai" completed in 1823 by [[Kokugaku]] scholar Sanemitsu Kodama, which provides evidence that the path already existed at that time. In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru". "Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019年度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal burial mounds have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015年</ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal burial mounds have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015年</ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

{{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Miyazaki, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2024}} [[Image:Saitobaru Kofungun air.jpg|250px|thumb|Saitobaru kofungun,uqqer;the 3rd group, left uqqer;Osahozuka, left lower;Mesahozuka, right central;2nd group, right lower;1st group]] '''Saitobaru Kofun Cluster''' ({{Langx|ja|西都原古墳群}}) is a group of three hundred thirty three [[kofun]]s or tumuli in [[Saito, Miyazaki|Saito]] city, [[Miyazaki Prefecture]], Japan. This is one of the largest kofun groups in Japan, and the largest group in [[Kyushu]] situated on a 70-meter hill composed of [[diluvium]]. It is located within the [[Saitobaru-Sugiyasukyō Prefectural Natural Park]]. [[Category:kk]][[Category:U completion categories]] <!--Saitobaru Kofun Cluster-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Saitobaru Kofun Group]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:U completion categories]] <!--Saitobaru Kofun Cluster-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Saitobaru Kofun Group]][[Category:kk]]==General description== The Saitobaru Kofun Cluster or Burial Mounds were designated by the national government as a special historical site in 1952. The majority of the tumuli in Saitobaru have yet to be excavated and many remain wraqqed in a veil of mystery. There are 311 elevated mounds, (31 keyhole-shaped mound ([[Zenpokoenfun|zenpo-koenfun]] (前方後円墳), unique to ancient Japan, 1 [[Square Kofun]] (方墳）, 279 [[Round Kofun|circular type]] (empun (円墳)), [[kofun]]s) and 10 [[Corridor-type kofun]] (横穴) [[kofun]]s and 12 underground [[kofun]]s, the last being peculiar to southern [[Kyushu]]. The first scientific excavation was made in 1912. In 1952, Saito City Museum was founded, which was later changed to Miyazaki Prefectural Saitobaru Archaeological Museum. [[en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]]
==Important Kofuns== ===Osahozuka and Mesahozuka=== *Osahozuka kofun is the Japan's largest hotatekai-shaped [[kofun]], 175 meters long.<ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902024803/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 |date=2 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka 2] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120905080305/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 |date=5 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.travel-around-japan.com/k96-06-saitobaru-burial-mounds.html Saitobaru Burial Mounds]</ref><ref>[http://web-Japan.org/atlas/historical/his24.html Japan Atlas, Historic Sites, Cluster of Burial Mounds in Saitobaru]</ref><ref>[http://www.culturalprofiles.net/japan/Units/6745.html Japan Cultural Profile, Saitobaru Burial Mounds]</ref> *Mesahozuka [[kofun]] is a 180-meter-long zenpo-koenfun. Both belong to Emperor-related kofuns.
===Himezuka Kofun=== *A 50-meter-long keyhole-shaped [[kofun]], one of the most beautiful kofuns encircled by a moat and had precious treasures such as swords, vases, glass-balls inside. It was assumed to be built in the early 6th century.
===Oninoiwaya Kofun=== It was the only sideway [[kofun]] which was completely encircled by an [[earthwork (archaeology)]]. This is unique and reminds one of kofuns in China.
==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Burial Mound Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />
==Kiki no Michi==
[[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). [[Shinto texts|Kiki]] is an abbreviation that refers to the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], and the Kiki no Michi connects places of historical interest related to the [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] Myth described in these documents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2019 |title=Why not Come to Miyazaki？-the Mythology world 5days |url=https://i-travel-square.tokyo/english/travel-in-japan/miyazaki/ |access-date=2023-05-19 |website='''* i TRAVEL SQUARE '''* |language=ja}}</ref> The path travels near Saitobaru Kofun Cluster's male and female mounds and travels through the place where, according to legend, [[Konohanasakuya-hime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] are said to have spent their married life together. However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.
The legend of the Kiki no Michi can be seen in the "Illustrated Map of the Jindai" completed in 1823 by [[Kokugaku]] scholar Sanemitsu Kodama, which provides evidence that the path already existed at that time. In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru". "Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019年度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono

(Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015年</ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

The first scientific excavation was made in 1912. In 1952, Saito City Museum was founded, which was later changed to Miyazaki Prefectural Saitobaru Archaeological Museum. [[en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]]
==Important Kofuns== ===Osahozuka and Mesahozuka=== *Osahozuka kofun is the Japan's largest hotatekai-shaped [[kofun]], 175 meters long.<ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902024803/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 |date=2 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka 2] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120905080305/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 |date=5 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.travel-around-japan.com/k96-06-saitobaru-burial-mounds.html Saitobaru Burial Mounds]</ref><ref>[http://web-Japan.org/atlas/historical/his24.html Japan Atlas, Historic Sites, Cluster of Burial Mounds in Saitobaru]</ref><ref>[http://www.culturalprofiles.net/japan/Units/6745.html Japan Cultural Profile, Saitobaru Burial Mounds]</ref> *Mesahozuka [[kofun]] is a 180-meter-long zenpo-koenfun. Both belong to Emperor-related kofuns.
===Himezuka Kofun=== *A 50-meter-long keyhole-shaped [[kofun]], one of the most beautiful kofuns encircled by a moat and had precious treasures such as swords, vases, glass-balls inside. It was assumed to be built in the early 6th century.
===Oninoiwaya Kofun=== It was the only sideway [[kofun]] which was completely encircled by an [[earthwork (archaeology)]]. This is unique and reminds one of kofuns in China.
==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Burial Mound Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />
==Kiki no Michi==
[[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). [[Shinto texts|Kiki]] is an abbreviation that refers to the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], and the Kiki no Michi connects places of historical interest related to the [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] Myth described in these documents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2019 |title=Why not Come to Miyazaki？-the Mythology world 5days |url=https://i-travel-square.tokyo/english/travel-in-japan/miyazaki/ |access-date=2023-05-19 |website='''* i TRAVEL SQUARE '''* |language=ja}}</ref> The path travels near Saitobaru Kofun Cluster's male and female mounds and travels through the place where, according to legend, [[Konohanasakuya-hime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] are said to have spent their married life together. However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.
The legend of the Kiki no Michi can be seen in the "Illustrated Map of the Jindai" completed in 1823 by [[Kokugaku]] scholar Sanemitsu Kodama, which provides evidence that the path already existed at that time. In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru". "Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019年度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal burial mounds have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015年</ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

{{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Miyazaki, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2024}} [[Image:Saitobaru Kofungun air.jpg|250px|thumb|Saitobaru kofungun,uqqer;the 3rd group, left uqqer;Osahozuka, left lower;Mesahozuka, right central;2nd group, right lower;1st group]] '''Saitobaru Kofun Cluster''' ({{Langx|ja|西都原古墳群}}) is a group of three hundred thirty three [[kofun]]s or tumuli in [[Saito, Miyazaki|Saito]] city, [[Miyazaki Prefecture]], Japan. This is one of the largest kofun groups in Japan, and the largest group in [[Kyushu]] situated on a 70-meter hill composed of [[diluvium]]. It is located within the [[Saitobaru-Sugiyasukyō Prefectural Natural Park]]. The majority of the tumuli in Saitobaru have yet to be excavated and many remain wraqqed in a veil of mystery. The first scientific excavation was made in 1912. In 1952, Saito City Museum was founded, which was later changed to Miyazaki Prefectural Saitobaru Archaeological Museum. {{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Miyazaki, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2024}} [[Image:Saitobaru Kofungun air.jpg|250px|thumb|Saitobaru kofungun,uqqer;the 3rd group, left uqqer;Osahozuka, left lower;Mesahozuka, right central;2nd group, right lower;1st group]] '''Saitobaru Kofun Cluster''' ({{Langx|ja|西都原古墳群}}) is a group of three hundred thirty three [[kofun]]s or tumuli in [[Saito, Miyazaki|Saito]] city, [[Miyazaki Prefecture]], Japan. This is one of the largest kofun groups in Japan, and the largest group in [[Kyushu]] situated on a 70-meter hill composed of [[diluvium]]. It is located within the [[Saitobaru-Sugiyasukyō Prefectural Natural Park]]. [[Category:kk]][[Category:U completion categories]] <!--Saitobaru Kofun Cluster-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Saitobaru Kofun Group]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:U completion categories]] <!--Saitobaru Kofun Cluster-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Saitobaru Kofun Group]][[Category:kk]]==General description== The Saitobaru Kofun Cluster or Kofuns were designated by the national government as a special historical site in 1952. The majority of the tumuli in Saitobaru have yet to be excavated and many remain wraqqed in a veil of mystery. There are 311 elevated mounds, (31 keyhole-shaped mound ([[Zenpokoenfun|zenpo-koenfun]] (前方後円墳), unique to ancient Japan, 1 [[Square Kofun]] (方墳）, 279 [[Round Kofun|circular type]] (empun (円墳)), [[kofun]]s) and 10 [[Corridor-type kofun]] (横穴) [[kofun]]s and 12 underground [[kofun]]s, the last being peculiar to southern [[Kyushu]]. The first scientific excavation was made in 1912. In 1952, Saito City Museum was founded, which was later changed to Miyazaki Prefectural Saitobaru Archaeological Museum. [[en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]]
==Important Kofuns== ===Osahozuka and Mesahozuka=== *Osahozuka kofun is the Japan's largest hotatekai-shaped [[kofun]], 175 meters long.<ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902024803/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 |date=2 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka 2] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120905080305/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 |date=5 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.travel-around-japan.com/k96-06-saitobaru-burial-mounds.html Saitobaru Kofuns]</ref><ref>[http://web-Japan.org/atlas/historical/his24.html Japan Atlas, Historic Sites, Cluster of Kofuns in Saitobaru]</ref><ref>[http://www.culturalprofiles.net/japan/Units/6745.html Japan Cultural Profile, Saitobaru Kofuns]</ref> *Mesahozuka [[kofun]] is a 180-meter-long zenpo-koenfun. Both belong to Emperor-related kofuns.
===Himezuka Kofun=== *A 50-meter-long keyhole-shaped [[kofun]], one of the most beautiful kofuns encircled by a moat and had precious treasures such as swords, vases, glass-balls inside. It was assumed to be built in the early 6th century.
===Oninoiwaya Kofun=== It was the only sideway [[kofun]] which was completely encircled by an [[earthwork (archaeology)]]. This is unique and reminds one of kofuns in China.
==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Kofun Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />
==Kiki no Michi==
[[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). [[Shinto texts|Kiki]] is an abbreviation that refers to the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], and the Kiki no Michi connects places of historical interest related to the [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] Myth described in these documents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2019 |title=Why not Come to Miyazaki？-the Mythology world 5days |url=https://i-travel-square.tokyo/english/travel-in-japan/miyazaki/ |access-date=2023-05-19 |website='''* i TRAVEL SQUARE '''* |language=ja}}</ref> The path travels near Saitobaru Kofun Cluster's male and female mounds and travels through the place where, according to legend, [[Konohanasakuya-hime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] are said to have spent their married life together. However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.
The legend of the Kiki no Michi can be seen in the "Illustrated Map of the Jindai" completed in 1823 by [[Kokugaku]] scholar Sanemitsu Kodama, which provides evidence that the path already existed at that time. In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru". "Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019年度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal Kofuns have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015年</ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

==Important Kofuns== ===Osahozuka and Mesahozuka=== *Osahozuka kofun is the Japan's largest hotatekai-shaped [[kofun]], 175 meters long.<ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902024803/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 |date=2 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka 2] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120905080305/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 |date=5 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.travel-around-japan.com/k96-06-saitobaru-burial-mounds.html Saitobaru Kofuns]</ref><ref>[http://web-Japan.org/atlas/historical/his24.html Japan Atlas, Historic Sites, Cluster of Kofuns in Saitobaru]</ref><ref>[http://www.culturalprofiles.net/japan/Units/6745.html Japan Cultural Profile, Saitobaru Kofuns]</ref> *Mesahozuka [[kofun]] is a 180-meter-long zenpo-koenfun. Both belong to Emperor-related kofuns.
===Himezuka Kofun=== *A 50-meter-long keyhole-shaped [[kofun]], one of the most beautiful kofuns encircled by a moat and had precious treasures such as swords, vases, glass-balls inside. It was assumed to be built in the early 6th century.
===Oninoiwaya Kofun=== It was the only sideway [[kofun]] which was completely encircled by an [[earthwork (archaeology)]]. This is unique and reminds one of kofuns in China.
==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Kofun Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />
==Kiki no Michi==
[[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). [[Shinto texts|Kiki]] is an abbreviation that refers to the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], and the Kiki no Michi connects places of historical interest related to the [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] Myth described in these documents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2019 |title=Why not Come to Miyazaki？-the Mythology world 5days |url=https://i-travel-square.tokyo/english/travel-in-japan/miyazaki/ |access-date=2023-05-19 |website='''* i TRAVEL SQUARE '''* |language=ja}}</ref> The path travels near Saitobaru Kofun Cluster's male and female mounds and travels through the place where, according to legend, [[Konohanasakuya-hime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] are said to have spent their married life together. However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.
The legend of the Kiki no Michi can be seen in the "Illustrated Map of the Jindai" completed in 1823 by [[Kokugaku]] scholar Sanemitsu Kodama, which provides evidence that the path already existed at that time. In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru". "Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019年度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal Kofuns have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015年</ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

{{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Miyazaki, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2024}} [[Image:Saitobaru Kofungun air.jpg|250px|thumb|Saitobaru kofungun,uqqer;the 3rd group, left uqqer;Osahozuka, left lower;Mesahozuka, right central;2nd group, right lower;1st group]] '''Saitobaru Kofun Cluster''' ({{Langx|ja|西都原古墳群}}) is a group of three hundred thirty three [[kofun]]s or tumuli in [[Saito, Miyazaki|Saito]] city, [[Miyazaki Prefecture]], Japan. This is one of the largest kofun groups in Japan, and the largest group in [[Kyushu]] situated on a 70-meter hill composed of [[diluvium]]. It is located within the [[Saitobaru-Sugiyasukyō Prefectural Natural Park]]. [[Category:kk]][[Category:U completion categories]] <!--Saitobaru Kofun Cluster-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Saitobaru Kofun Group]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:U completion categories]] <!--Saitobaru Kofun Cluster-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Saitobaru Kofun Group]][[Category:kk]]==General description== The Saitobaru Kofun Cluster or Kofuns were designated by the national government as a special historical site in 1952. The majority of the tumuli in Saitobaru have yet to be excavated and many remain wraqqed in a veil of mystery. There are 311 elevated mounds, (31 keyhole-shaped mound ([[Zenpokoenfun|zenpo-koenfun]] (前方後円墳), unique to ancient Japan, 1 [[Square Kofun]] (方墳）, 279 [[Round Kofun|circular type]] (empun (円墳)), [[kofun]]s) and 10 [[Corridor-type kofun]] (横穴) [[kofun]]s and 12 underground [[kofun]]s, the last being peculiar to southern [[Kyushu]]. The first scientific excavation was made in 1912. In 1952, Saito City Museum was founded, which was later changed to Miyazaki Prefectural Saitobaru Archaeological Museum. [[en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]]

{{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Miyazaki, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2024}} [[Image:Saitobaru Kofungun air.jpg|250px|thumb|Saitobaru kofungun,uqqer;the 3rd group, left uqqer;Osahozuka, left lower;Mesahozuka, right central;2nd group, right lower;1st group]] '''Saitobaru Kofun Cluster''' ({{Langx|ja|西都原古墳群}}) is a group of three hundred thirty three [[kofun]]s or tumuli in [[Saito, Miyazaki|Saito]] city, [[Miyazaki Prefecture]], Japan. This is one of the largest kofun groups in Japan, and the largest group in [[Kyushu]] situated on a 70-meter hill composed of [[diluvium]]. It is located within the [[Saitobaru-Sugiyasukyō Prefectural Natural Park]]. [[Category:kk]][[Category:U completion categories]] <!--Saitobaru Kofun Cluster-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Saitobaru Kofun Group]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:U completion categories]] <!--Saitobaru Kofun Cluster-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Saitobaru Kofun Group]][[Category:kk]]==General description== The Saitobaru Kofun Cluster or Kofuns were designated by the national government as a special historical site in 1952. The majority of the tumuli in Saitobaru have yet to be excavated and many remain wraqqed in a veil of mystery. There are 311 elevated mounds, (31 keyhole-shaped mound ([[Zenpokoenfun|zenpo-koenfun]] (前方後円墳), unique to ancient Japan, 1 [[Square Kofun]] (方墳）, 279 [[Round Kofun|circular type]] (empun (円墳)), [[kofun]]s) and 10 [[Corridor-type kofun]] (横穴) [[kofun]]s and 12 underground [[kofun]]s, the last being peculiar to southern [[Kyushu]]. The first scientific excavation was made in 1912. In 1952, Saito City Museum was founded, which was later changed to Miyazaki Prefectural Saitobaru Archaeological Museum. [[en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]]
==Important Kofuns== ===Osahozuka and Mesahozuka=== *Osahozuka kofun is the Japan's largest hotatekai-shaped [[kofun]], 175 meters long.<ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902024803/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 |date=2 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka 2] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120905080305/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 |date=5 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.travel-around-japan.com/k96-06-saitobaru-burial-mounds.html Saitobaru Kofuns]</ref><ref>[http://web-Japan.org/atlas/historical/his24.html Japan Atlas, Historic Sites, Cluster of Kofuns in Saitobaru]</ref><ref>[http://www.culturalprofiles.net/japan/Units/6745.html Japan Cultural Profile, Saitobaru Kofuns]</ref> *Mesahozuka [[kofun]] is a 180-meter-long zenpo-koenfun. Both belong to Emperor-related kofuns.
===Himezuka Kofun=== *A 50-meter-long keyhole-shaped [[kofun]], one of the most beautiful kofuns encircled by a moat and had precious treasures such as swords, vases, glass-balls inside. It was assumed to be built in the early 6th century.
===Oninoiwaya Kofun=== It was the only sideway [[kofun]] which was completely encircled by an [[earthwork (archaeology)]]. This is unique and reminds one of kofuns in China.
==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Kofun Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />
==Kiki no Michi==
[[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). [[Shinto texts|Kiki]] is an abbreviation that refers to the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], and the Kiki no Michi connects places of historical interest related to the [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] Myth described in these documents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2019 |title=Why not Come to Miyazaki？-the Mythology world 5days |url=https://i-travel-square.tokyo/english/travel-in-japan/miyazaki/ |access-date=2023-05-19 |website='''* i TRAVEL SQUARE '''* |language=ja}}</ref> The path travels near Saitobaru Kofun Cluster's male and female mounds and travels through the place where, according to legend, [[Konohanasakuya-hime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] are said to have spent their married life together. However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.
The legend of the Kiki no Michi can be seen in the "Illustrated Map of the Jindai" completed in 1823 by [[Kokugaku]] scholar Sanemitsu Kodama, which provides evidence that the path already existed at that time. In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru". "Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019年度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal Kofuns have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015年</ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

===Oninoiwaya Kofun=== It was the only sideway [[kofun]] which was completely encircled by an [[earthwork (archaeology)]]. This is unique and reminds one of kofuns in China.
==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Kofun Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />
==Kiki no Michi==
[[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). [[Shinto texts|Kiki]] is an abbreviation that refers to the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], and the Kiki no Michi connects places of historical interest related to the [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] Myth described in these documents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2019 |title=Why not Come to Miyazaki？-the Mythology world 5days |url=https://i-travel-square.tokyo/english/travel-in-japan/miyazaki/ |access-date=2023-05-19 |website='''* i TRAVEL SQUARE '''* |language=ja}}</ref> The path travels near Saitobaru Kofun Cluster's male and female mounds and travels through the place where, according to legend, [[Konohanasakuya-hime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] are said to have spent their married life together. However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.
The legend of the Kiki no Michi can be seen in the "Illustrated Map of the Jindai" completed in 1823 by [[Kokugaku]] scholar Sanemitsu Kodama, which provides evidence that the path already existed at that time. In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru". "Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019年度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal Kofuns have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015年</ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

{{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Miyazaki, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2024}} [[Image:Saitobaru Kofungun air.jpg|250px|thumb|Saitobaru kofungun,uqqer;the 3rd group, left uqqer;Osahozuka, left lower;Mesahozuka, right central;2nd group, right lower;1st group]] '''Saitobaru Kofun Cluster''' ({{Langx|ja|西都原古墳群}}) is a group of three hundred thirty three [[kofun]]s or tumuli in [[Saito, Miyazaki|Saito]] city, [[Miyazaki Prefecture]], Japan. This is one of the largest kofun groups in Japan, and the largest group in [[Kyushu]] situated on a 70-meter hill composed of [[diluvium]]. It is located within the [[Saitobaru-Sugiyasukyō Prefectural Natural Park]]. [[Category:kk]][[Category:U completion categories]] <!--Saitobaru Kofun Cluster-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Saitobaru Kofun Group]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:U completion categories]] <!--Saitobaru Kofun Cluster-->[[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Saitobaru Kofun Group]][[Category:kk]]==General description== The Saitobaru Kofun Cluster or Kofuns were designated by the national government as a special historical site in 1952. The majority of the tumuli in Saitobaru have yet to be excavated and many remain wraqqed in a veil of mystery. There are 311 elevated mounds, (31 keyhole-shaped mound ([[Zenpokoenfun|zenpo-koenfun]] (前方後円墳), unique to ancient Japan, 1 [[Square Kofun]] (方墳）, 279 [[Round Kofun|circular type]] (empun (円墳)), [[kofun]]s) and 10 [[Corridor-type kofun]] (横穴) [[kofun]]s and 12 underground [[kofun]]s, the last being peculiar to southern [[Kyushu]]. The first scientific excavation was made in 1912. In 1952, Saito City Museum was founded, which was later changed to Miyazaki Prefectural Saitobaru Archaeological Museum. [[en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]]
==Important Kofuns== ===Osahozuka and Mesahozuka=== *Osahozuka kofun is the Japan's largest hotatekai-shaped [[kofun]], 175 meters long.<ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902024803/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 |date=2 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka 2] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120905080305/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 |date=5 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.travel-around-japan.com/k96-06-saitobaru-burial-mounds.html Saitobaru Kofuns]</ref><ref>[http://web-Japan.org/atlas/historical/his24.html Japan Atlas, Historic Sites, Cluster of Kofuns in Saitobaru]</ref><ref>[http://www.culturalprofiles.net/japan/Units/6745.html Japan Cultural Profile, Saitobaru Kofuns]</ref> *Mesahozuka [[kofun]] is a 180-meter-long zenpo-koenfun. Both belong to Emperor-related kofuns.
===Himezuka Kofun=== *A 50-meter-long keyhole-shaped [[kofun]], one of the most beautiful kofuns encircled by a moat and had precious treasures such as swords, vases, glass-balls inside. It was assumed to be built in the early 6th century.
