{{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Miyazaki, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2024}} [[Image:Saitobaru Kofungun air.jpg|250px|thumb|Saitobaru kofungun,u11er;the 3rd group, left u11er;Osahozuka, left lower;Mesahozuka, right central;2nd group, right lower;1st group]] '''Saitobaru Kofun Cluster''' ({{Langx|ja|西都原古墳群}}) is a group of three hundred thirty three [[kofun]]s or tumuli in [[Saito, Miyazaki|Saito]] city, [[Miyazaki Prefecture]], Japan. This is one of the largest kofun groups in Japan, and the largest group in [[Kyushu]] situated on a 70-meter hill composed of [[diluvium]]. It is located within the [[Saitobaru-Sugiyasukyō Prefectural Natural Park]]. <nowiki>==General description==</nowiki> The Saitobaru Kofun Cluster or Kofuns were designated by the national government as a special historical site in 1952. The majority of the tumuli in Saitobaru have yet to be excavated and many remain wra11ed in a veil of mystery. There are 311 elevated mounds, (31 keyhole-shaped mound ([[Zenpokoenfun|zenpo-koenfun]] (前方後円墳), unique to ancient Japan, 1 [[Square Kofun]] (方墳）, 279 [[Round Kofun|circular type]] (empun (円墳)), [[kofun]]s) and 10 [[Cave tomb|Cave tombs]] (横穴) [[kofun]]s and 12 underground [[kofun]]s, the last being peculiar to southern [[Kyushu]]. The first scientific excavation was made in 1912. In 1952, Saito City Museum was founded, which was later changed to Miyazaki Prefectural Saitobaru Archaeological Museum.
==Important Kofuns== ===Osahozuka and Mesahozuka=== *Osahozuka kofun is the Japan's largest hotatekai-shaped [[kofun]], 175 meters long.<ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902024803/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 |date=2 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka 2] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120905080305/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 |date=5 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.travel-around-japan.com/k96-06-saitobaru-burial-mounds.html Saitobaru Kofuns]</ref><ref>[http://web-Japan.org/atlas/historical/his24.html Japan Atlas, Historic Sites, Cluster of Kofuns in Saitobaru]</ref><ref>[http://www.culturalprofiles.net/japan/Units/6745.html Japan Cultural Profile, Saitobaru Kofuns]</ref> *Mesahozuka [[kofun]] is a 180-meter-long zenpo-koenfun. Both belong to Emperor-related kofuns.
===Himezuka Kofun=== *A 50-meter-long keyhole-shaped [[kofun]], one of the most beautiful kofuns encircled by a moat and had precious treasures such as swords, vases, glass-balls inside. It was assumed to be built in the early 6th century.
===Oninoiwaya Kofun=== It was the only sideway [[kofun]] which was completely encircled by an [[earthwork (archaeology)]]. This is unique and reminds one of kofuns in China.
==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Kofun Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />

The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019th year 度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal Kofuns have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015th year </ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

{{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Miyazaki, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2024}} [[Image:Saitobaru Kofungun air.jpg|250px|thumb|Saitobaru kofungun,u11er;the 3rd group, left u11er;Osahozuka, left lower;Mesahozuka, right central;2nd group, right lower;1st group]] '''Saitobaru Kofun Cluster''' ({{Langx|ja|西都原古墳群}}) is a group of three hundred thirty three [[kofun]]s or tumuli in [[Saito, Miyazaki|Saito]] city, [[Miyazaki Prefecture]], Japan. This is one of the largest kofun groups in Japan, and the largest group in [[Kyushu]] situated on a 70-meter hill composed of [[diluvium]]. It is located within the [[Saitobaru-Sugiyasukyō Prefectural Natural Park]]. <nowiki>==General description==</nowiki> The Saitobaru Kofun Cluster or Kofuns were designated by the national government as a special historical site in 1952. The majority of the tumuli in Saitobaru have yet to be excavated and many remain wra11ed in a veil of mystery. There are 311 elevated mounds, (31 keyhole-shaped mound ([[Zenpokoenfun|zenpo-koenfun]] (前方後円墳), unique to ancient Japan, 1 [[Square Kofun]] (方墳）, 279 [[Round Kofun|circular type]] (empun (円墳)), [[kofun]]s) and 10 [[Cave tomb|Cave tombs]] (横穴) [[kofun]]s and 12 underground [[kofun]]s, the last being peculiar to southern [[Kyushu]]. The first scientific excavation was made in 1912. In 1952, Saito City Museum was founded, which was later changed to Miyazaki Prefectural Saitobaru Archaeological Museum.
==Important Kofuns== ===Osahozuka and Mesahozuka=== *Osahozuka kofun is the Japan's largest hotatekai-shaped [[kofun]], 175 meters long.<ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902024803/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 |date=2 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka 2] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120905080305/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 |date=5 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.travel-around-japan.com/k96-06-saitobaru-burial-mounds.html Saitobaru Kofuns]</ref><ref>[http://web-Japan.org/atlas/historical/his24.html Japan Atlas, Historic Sites, Cluster of Kofuns in Saitobaru]</ref><ref>[http://www.culturalprofiles.net/japan/Units/6745.html Japan Cultural Profile, Saitobaru Kofuns]</ref> *Mesahozuka [[kofun]] is a 180-meter-long zenpo-koenfun. Both belong to Emperor-related kofuns.
===Himezuka Kofun=== *A 50-meter-long keyhole-shaped [[kofun]], one of the most beautiful kofuns encircled by a moat and had precious treasures such as swords, vases, glass-balls inside. It was assumed to be built in the early 6th century.
===Oninoiwaya Kofun=== It was the only sideway [[kofun]] which was completely encircled by an [[earthwork (archaeology)]]. This is unique and reminds one of kofuns in China.
==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Kofun Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />
==Kiki no Michi==
[[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). [[Shinto texts|Kiki]] is an abbreviation that refers to the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], and the Kiki no Michi connects places of historical interest related to the [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] Myth described in these documents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2019 |title=Why not Come to Miyazaki？-the Mythology world 5days |url=https://i-travel-square.tokyo/english/travel-in-japan/miyazaki/ |access-date=2023-05-19 |website='''* i TRAVEL SQUARE '''* |language=ja}}</ref> The path travels near Saitobaru Kofun Cluster's male and female mounds and travels through the place where, according to legend, [[Konohanasakuya-hime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] are said to have spent their married life together. However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.
The legend of the Kiki no Michi can be seen in the "Illustrated Map of the Jindai" completed in 1823 by [[Kokugaku]] scholar Sanemitsu Kodama, which provides evidence that the path already existed at that time. In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru". "Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019th year 度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal Kofuns have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015th year </ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

"Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019th year 度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal Kofuns have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015th year </ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

{{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Miyazaki, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2024}} [[Image:Saitobaru Kofungun air.jpg|250px|thumb|Saitobaru kofungun,u11er;the 3rd group, left u11er;Osahozuka, left lower;Mesahozuka, right central;2nd group, right lower;1st group]] '''Saitobaru Kofun Cluster''' ({{Langx|ja|西都原古墳群}}) is a group of three hundred thirty three [[kofun]]s or tumuli in [[Saito, Miyazaki|Saito]] city, [[Miyazaki Prefecture]], Japan. This is one of the largest kofun groups in Japan, and the largest group in [[Kyushu]] situated on a 70-meter hill composed of [[diluvium]]. It is located within the [[Saitobaru-Sugiyasukyō Prefectural Natural Park]]. <nowiki>==General description==</nowiki> The Saitobaru Kofun Cluster or Kofuns were designated by the national government as a special historical site in 1952. The majority of the tumuli in Saitobaru have yet to be excavated and many remain wra11ed in a veil of mystery. There are 311 elevated mounds, (31 keyhole-shaped mound ([[Zenpokoenfun|zenpo-koenfun]] (前方後円墳), unique to ancient Japan, 1 [[Square Kofun]] (方墳）, 279 [[Round Kofun|circular type]] (empun (円墳)), [[kofun]]s) and 10 [[Cave tomb|Cave tombs]] (横穴) [[kofun]]s and 12 underground [[kofun]]s, the last being peculiar to southern [[Kyushu]]. The first scientific excavation was made in 1912. In 1952, Saito City Museum was founded, which was later changed to Miyazaki Prefectural Saitobaru Archaeological Museum.
==Important Kofuns== ===Osahozuka and Mesahozuka=== *Osahozuka kofun is the Japan's largest hotatekai-shaped [[kofun]], 175 meters long.<ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902024803/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 |date=2 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka 2] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120905080305/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 |date=5 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.travel-around-japan.com/k96-06-saitobaru-burial-mounds.html Saitobaru Kofuns]</ref><ref>[http://web-Japan.org/atlas/historical/his24.html Japan Atlas, Historic Sites, Cluster of Kofuns in Saitobaru]</ref><ref>[http://www.culturalprofiles.net/japan/Units/6745.html Japan Cultural Profile, Saitobaru Kofuns]</ref> *Mesahozuka [[kofun]] is a 180-meter-long zenpo-koenfun. Both belong to Emperor-related kofuns.
===Himezuka Kofun=== *A 50-meter-long keyhole-shaped [[kofun]], one of the most beautiful kofuns encircled by a moat and had precious treasures such as swords, vases, glass-balls inside. It was assumed to be built in the early 6th century.
===Oninoiwaya Kofun=== It was the only sideway [[kofun]] which was completely encircled by an [[earthwork (archaeology)]]. This is unique and reminds one of kofuns in China.
==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Kofun Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />
==Kiki no Michi==
[[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). [[Shinto texts|Kiki]] is an abbreviation that refers to the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], and the Kiki no Michi connects places of historical interest related to the [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] Myth described in these documents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2019 |title=Why not Come to Miyazaki？-the Mythology world 5days |url=https://i-travel-square.tokyo/english/travel-in-japan/miyazaki/ |access-date=2023-05-19 |website='''* i TRAVEL SQUARE '''* |language=ja}}</ref> The path travels near Saitobaru Kofun Cluster's male and female mounds and travels through the place where, according to legend, [[Konohanasakuya-hime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] are said to have spent their married life together. However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.
The legend of the Kiki no Michi can be seen in the "Illustrated Map of the Jindai" completed in 1823 by [[Kokugaku]] scholar Sanemitsu Kodama, which provides evidence that the path already existed at that time. In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru". "Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019th year 度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal Kofuns have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015th year </ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

{{日本の古墳 |名称=西都原古墳群 |所属='''西都原古墳群''' |所在地=[[宮崎県]][[西都市]]大字三宅ほか |ISO = JP-45 |形状= |埋葬施設= |築造年代=4世紀初頭～7世紀前半 |規模=高塚墳311基（[[前方後円墳]]31基、[[方墳]]1基、[[円墳]]279基） |出土品= |被葬者= |指定文化財= 国の[[特別史跡]]「西都原古墳群」 |画像= [[Image:Saitobaru Kofungun air.jpg|250px|]]
西都原古墳群
{{国土航空写真}} |特記事項= |地図=Japan Miyazaki |アイコン=古墳群 |ラベル=西都原
古墳群 |ラベル位置 = bottom }} '''西都原古墳群'''（さいとばるこふんぐん）は、[[宮崎県]][[西都市]]三宅・童子丸・右松にある[[古墳群]]。国の[[特別史跡]]に指定されている。 [[標高]]70メートル程の[[洪積層]]の[[台地]]上に分布する日本最大級の古墳群である。第81号墳を現状最古として、[[4世紀]]初頭{{Sfn|大阪府立近つ飛鳥博物館|2012|p=40}}から[[7世紀]]前半にかけての築造と推定されている。 == 概要 == 現在、高塚墳319基が現存し、その内訳は前方後円墳31基、方墳2基、円墳286基{{Cite web|和書|title=宮崎県立西都原考古博物館｜西都原古墳群の概要|url=http://saito-muse.pref.miyazaki.jp/web/guidance.html|website=saito-muse.pref.miyazaki.jp|accessdate=2019-09-24}}であるが、他に[[横穴墓]]が10基、[[南九州]]特有の[[地下式横穴墓]]が12基確認されている。 [[1912年]]（[[大正]]元年）から[[1917年]]（大正6年）にかけて日本で初めて本格的学術調査が行われた地としても有名である。調査は[[1912年]]（大正元年）12月25日から翌[[1913年]]（大正2年）1月6日に第1次調査、同年5月に第2次調査、[[1914年]]（大正3年）8月に第3次調査、[[1915年]]（大正4年）1月に第4次調査、[[1916年]]（大正5年）1月に第5次調査、同年12月から翌[[1917年]]（大正6年）1月に第6次調査が実施された。 [[1914年]]（大正3年）、出土品を収蔵するため宮崎県立史跡研究所が設立された。同研究所は後に市に移管され、[[1952年]]（昭和27年）に[[博物館法]]指定を受けた西都市立博物館となった時期を経て、現在は再び県立の[[宮崎県立西都原考古博物館|西都原考古博物館]]として出土品の保管と展示を行っている。 [[1934年]]（[[昭和]]9年）に国の[[史跡]]に、[[1952年]]（昭和27年）に国の[[特別史跡]]に指定され、[[1966年]]（昭和41年）から[[1968年]]（昭和43年）にかけて、[[風土記の丘]]第1号として整備が進められた。 ==分布== 西都原古墳群は地形的に西都原台地上と、西都原台地と市街地との間に位置する中間台地上の二地域に区分でき、その中で更に11の集団、あるいは10～13の支群{{Sfn|宮崎県立西都原考古博物館|2015|p=18}}に分けることができる。 File:Oni-no-iwaya kofun oni-no-iwaya & Mesahozuka.JPG|手前に鬼の窟古墳、左奥に[[男狭穂塚]]・[[女狭穂塚]]を遠望 ===西都原台地上=== *第一集団（第1-A支群・第1-B支群） :台地の東南部地帯。古墳群内で最大の群集地域。前方後円墳7基を含む計91基。[[#姫塚（202号墳）|姫塚（202号墳）]]など。 *第二集団（第2-A支群） :台地の東側縁辺部に一列に形成。前方後円墳10基を含む計36基。 *第三集団（第2-B支群・第3-A支群・第3-B支群） :台地の北部に形成。前方後円墳1基を含む計86基。 *第四集団（丸山支群） :台地上でも一段高い丸山丘陵の東側裾部に築かれた「[[男狭穂塚古墳]]」「[[女狭穂塚古墳]]」とその陪塚。 *第五集団（第1-B支群） :台地のほぼ中央に位置する、古墳群内唯一の横穴式石室墳「[[#鬼の窟古墳（206号墳）|鬼の窟古墳（206号墳）]]」とその周辺の3基。1995年（平成7年）の調査で[[横穴墓]]（酒元ノ上横穴墓群）も確認。 *第六集団（寺原第1支群） :台地の西側、寺原丘陵一帯に築かれた古墳。前方後円墳3基を含む計16基。 *第七集団（寺原第2支群） :寺原集落地域内の古墳。前方後円墳1基を含む計12基。ただし、この前方後円墳は道路によって切断されている。 ===中間台地上=== *第八集団（堂ヶ島支群） :堂ヶ島微高地・童子丸台地上一帯の円墳。 *第九集団（鷲田支群） :[[宮崎県立妻高等学校]]及び[[日向国分寺]]のある諏訪地域の古墳。前方後円墳2基を含む計20基。 *第十集団（尾筋支群） :三宅集落丘陵の上・下尾筋地域の古墳。前方後円墳5基を含む計18基。 *第十一集団（鳥子支群） :三宅丘陵南部の沖積層である鳥子地域に築かれた古墳。前方後円墳1基を含む計4基。 ==西都原台地上の主な古墳== === 男狭穂塚・女狭穂塚 === {{main|男狭穂塚古墳|女狭穂塚古墳}} 男狭穂塚（おさほづか、175メートル）は日本最大の帆立貝形古墳。女狭穂塚（めさほづか、180メートル）は九州最大の[[前方後円墳]]。共に[[宮内庁]][[陵墓参考地]]であり、特別史跡の指定範囲には含まれない全長は調査年次によって様々な数値が発表されているが、ここでは[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/sight/kanko/kofun.html 西都市　特別史跡　西都原古墳群]による。[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siseki/index.html 西都市の文化財]。 === 姫塚（202号墳） === 姫塚は「第1集団（第1-B支群）」の西端に位置する前方後円墳で、墳長50.2メートル、前方部幅30.8メートル、前方部高さ5.25メートル、後円部径28.4メートル、後円部高さ6.0メートルを測る。その形状の美しさから姫塚（ひめづか）と呼ばれ、周囲には周湟（周濠）が巡らされている。確認された埋葬主体は木棺直葬である。[[大正時代]]に発掘された30基のうちの一つで、[[直刀]]3本、[[刀子]]（とうす）1本、[[須恵器]]9個、ガラス製小玉、水晶製切子玉などが出土した吉本正典 編著『[https://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/ja/search/item/7779?all=%E8%A5%BF%E9%83%BD%E5%8E%9F%E5%8F%A4%E5%A2%B3%E7%BE%A4202%E5%8F%B7%E5%A2%B3&include_file=include 特別史跡 西都原古墳群 発掘調査・保存整備報告書ⅩⅢ]』宮崎教育委員会、2010。前方部の発達具合や大正年間の発掘の際の出土品から築造年代は[[6世紀]]初頭（古墳時代後期）と考えられている。 === 鬼の窟古墳（206号墳） === {{main|鬼の窟古墳 (西都市)}} [[File:Oni-no-iwaya kofun zenkei.JPG|thumb|200px|right|鬼の窟古墳]] 鬼の窟古墳（おにのいわやこふん）は西都原古墳群内で唯一、埋葬施設に[[横穴式石室]]を採用している古墳である。[[鬼]]が一夜で造りあげたとする[[伝説]]が残ることが名の由来となっている。石室入り口付近に生えていた[[クスノキ|楠]]により石室崩壊の危機にあったため、解体修復作業が行われ、その際同時に発掘調査が実施された。石室内の水を排出するための[[暗渠]]の存在や[[土塁]]が完全に古墳を一周していたこと、追葬が行われていたことなどが明らかとなった。古墳の周囲に土塁を巡らしているのは[[中華人民共和国]]・[[朝鮮半島]]ではよく見られるが、国内では[[石舞台古墳]]が類似するのみで、関係が注目される。 File:Oni-no-iwaya kofun sekishitsu.JPG|鬼の窟古墳石室 === その他 === 13号墳、35号墳、56号墳、72号墳、81号墳、100号墳、169号墳（飯盛塚）、170号墳（雑掌塚）、171号墳、173号墳、265号墳 西都原13号墳 三角縁獣帯三神三獣鏡.JPG|13号墳 三角縁獣帯三神三獣鏡
{{small|宮崎県立西都原考古博物館展示。}} 西都原169号墳 衝角付冑形埴輪 (J-34665).JPG|169号墳 衝角付冑形埴輪
{{small|東京国立博物館展示。}} Saitobaru-kofungun 3rd kofungun.JPG|第3古墳群 Saitobaru-kofungun yokoana-bogun.JPG|酒元ノ上横穴墓群 == 文化財 == === 国の特別史跡 === * 西都原古墳群 *: 1934年（昭和9年）5月1日、国の史跡に指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|2918|西都原古墳群}}。 *: 1952年（昭和27年）3月29日、国の特別史跡に指定。 *: 1972年（昭和47年）9月7日、1997年（平成9年）3月6日、1998年（平成10年）9月2日、2002年（平成14年）9月20日に特別史跡範囲の追加指定。 === 重要文化財（国指定） === [[ファイル:西都原古墳群出土 埴輪 子持家.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|埴輪 子持家}}{{small|[[東京国立博物館]]展示。}}]] [[ファイル:西都原古墳群出土 埴輪 船 (J-21498)-2.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|埴輪 船}}{{small|東京国立博物館展示。}}]] * 埴輪家（考古資料） - 東京国立博物館保管。1958年（昭和33年）2月8日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|9776|埴輪家}}。 * 埴輪船（考古資料） - 東京国立博物館保管。1958年（昭和33年）2月8日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|9777|埴輪船}}。 === 関連文化財 === * 日向国西都原古墳出土金銅馬具類 *: 国宝（考古資料）。指定名称に「西都原古墳出土」とあるが、実際には[[1897年]]（明治30年）頃の百塚原古墳群（西都原の西方）からの出土とされる。明細は以下。[[五島美術館]]（東京都）所蔵、宮崎県立西都原考古博物館にレプリカ所蔵。 *: 1935年（昭和10年）4月30日に[[国宝保存法]]に基づく旧国宝（1950年の[[文化財保護法]]施行後は重要文化財）に指定、1956年（昭和31年）6月28日に文化財保護法に基づく国宝に指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|853|日向国西都原古墳出土金銅馬具類}} ** 金銅鞍橋金具（くらぼねかなぐ）残闕 1背分 ** 金銅透彫杏葉（ぎょうよう）3枚 ** 金銅無地杏葉 4枚 ** 金銅透彫雲珠（うず）1箇 ** 金銅無地雲珠 1箇 ** 金銅透彫辻金物 9箇 ** 金銅無地辻金物 6箇 ** 金銅透彫散金物 16箇 ** 金銅透彫轡鏡板（くつわかがみいた）2箇 ** 金銅鉸具（かこ）1箇 ==関連施設== [[File:Saitobaru Archaeology Museum.jpg|サムネイル|180px|[[宮崎県立西都原考古博物館|西都原考古博物館]]]] *[[宮崎県立西都原考古博物館]] *西都市歴史民俗資料館{{Cite web|和書|title=西都市歴史民俗資料館について|url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/0305_1703310000000006.html|website=西都市|accessdate=2019-09-24|language=ja|last=西都市}} == 周辺の遺跡 == *[[日向国分寺]] *[[常心塚古墳]] *[[千畑古墳]] *[[児屋根塚古墳]]（[[茶臼原古墳群]]） *穂北横穴墓群 *三納古墳群 - 松本塚古墳 *[[三財古墳群]] *[[新田原古墳群]] == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == *{{Cite book|和書|author=大阪府立近つ飛鳥博物館|title=大阪府立近つ飛鳥博物館図録58 南九州とヤマト王権 -日向・大隅の古墳- 大阪府立近つ飛鳥博物館平成24年度秋季特別展|chapter=西都原古墳群|pages=38-59|publisher=[[大阪府立近つ飛鳥博物館]]|year=2012-09-29|date=2012-09-29|ncid=BB10393330|ref=harv}} * {{Cite book|和書|author=宮崎県立西都原考古博物館|authorlink=宮崎県立西都原考古博物館|title=生目・西都原・新田原－日向における古墳時代の首長墓系譜を読む－（平成27年度特別展図録）|chapter=西都原古墳群|pages=17-32|publisher=宮崎県立西都原考古博物館|year=2015-07-18|date=2015-07-18|ncid=BB1925634X|ref=harv}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=東憲章|year=2017|chapter=|title=古墳時代の南九州の雄 西都原古墳群（シリーズ「遺跡を学ぶ」121）|publisher=新泉社|pages=|isbn=978-4787718310|ref={{Harvid|東憲章|2017年}}}} ==外部リンク== * [http://saito-muse.pref.miyazaki.jp/ 宮崎県立西都原考古博物館] * {{Commonscat-inline}} {{日本の都市公園100選}} {{coord|32|7|4|N|131|23|22|E|region:JP-45|display=title}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:さいとはるこふんくん}} [[Category:西都原古墳群| ]] [[Category:特別史跡]] [[Category:宮崎県にある国指定の史跡]] [[Category:東京都区部の重要文化財]]

{{日本の古墳 |名称=西都原古墳群 |所属='''西都原古墳群''' |所在地=[[宮崎県]][[西都市]]大字三宅ほか |ISO = JP-45 |形状= |埋葬施設= |築造年代=4世紀初頭～7世紀前半 |規模=高塚墳311基（[[前方後円墳]]31基、[[方墳]]1基、[[円墳]]279基） |出土品= |被葬者= |指定文化財= 国の[[特別史跡]]「西都原古墳群」 |画像= [[Image:Saitobaru Kofungun air.jpg|250px|]]
西都原古墳群
{{国土航空写真}} |特記事項= |地図=Japan Miyazaki |アイコン=古墳群 |ラベル=西都原
古墳群 |ラベル位置 = bottom }} '''西都原古墳群'''（さいとばるこふんぐん）は、[[宮崎県]][[西都市]]三宅・童子丸・右松にある[[古墳群]]。国の[[特別史跡]]に指定されている。 [[標高]]70メートル程の[[洪積層]]の[[台地]]上に分布する日本最大級の古墳群である。第81号墳を現状最古として、[[4世紀]]初頭{{Sfn|大阪府立近つ飛鳥博物館|2012|p=40}}から[[7世紀]]前半にかけての築造と推定されている。 == 概要 == 現在、高塚墳319基が現存し、その内訳は前方後円墳31基、方墳2基、円墳286基{{Cite web|和書|title=宮崎県立西都原考古博物館｜西都原古墳群の概要|url=http://saito-muse.pref.miyazaki.jp/web/guidance.html|website=saito-muse.pref.miyazaki.jp|accessdate=2019-09-24}}であるが、他に[[横穴墓]]が10基、[[南九州]]特有の[[地下式横穴墓]]が12基確認されている。 [[1912年]]（[[大正]]元年）から[[1917年]]（大正6年）にかけて日本で初めて本格的学術調査が行われた地としても有名である。調査は[[1912年]]（大正元年）12月25日から翌[[1913年]]（大正2年）1月6日に第1次調査、同年5月に第2次調査、[[1914年]]（大正3年）8月に第3次調査、[[1915年]]（大正4年）1月に第4次調査、[[1916年]]（大正5年）1月に第5次調査、同年12月から翌[[1917年]]（大正6年）1月に第6次調査が実施された。 [[1914年]]（大正3年）、出土品を収蔵するため宮崎県立史跡研究所が設立された。同研究所は後に市に移管され、[[1952年]]（昭和27年）に[[博物館法]]指定を受けた西都市立博物館となった時期を経て、現在は再び県立の[[宮崎県立西都原考古博物館|西都原考古博物館]]として出土品の保管と展示を行っている。 [[1934年]]（[[昭和]]9年）に国の[[史跡]]に、[[1952年]]（昭和27年）に国の[[特別史跡]]に指定され、[[1966年]]（昭和41年）から[[1968年]]（昭和43年）にかけて、[[風土記の丘]]第1号として整備が進められた。 ==分布== 西都原古墳群は地形的に西都原台地上と、西都原台地と市街地との間に位置する中間台地上の二地域に区分でき、その中で更に11の集団、あるいは10～13の支群{{Sfn|宮崎県立西都原考古博物館|2015|p=18}}に分けることができる。 File:Oni-no-iwaya kofun oni-no-iwaya & 発掘調査・保存整備報告書ⅩⅢ]』宮崎教育委員会、2010。前方部の発達具合や大正年間の発掘の際の出土品から築造年代は[[6世紀]]初頭（古墳時代後期）と考えられている。 === 鬼の窟古墳（206号墳） === {{main|鬼の窟古墳 (西都市)}} [[File:Oni-no-iwaya kofun zenkei.JPG|thumb|200px|right|鬼の窟古墳]] 鬼の窟古墳（おにのいわやこふん）は西都原古墳群内で唯一、埋葬施設に[[横穴式石室]]を採用している古墳である。[[鬼]]が一夜で造りあげたとする[[伝説]]が残ることが名の由来となっている。石室入り口付近に生えていた[[クスノキ|楠]]により石室崩壊の危機にあったため、解体修復作業が行われ、その際同時に発掘調査が実施された。石室内の水を排出するための[[暗渠]]の存在や[[土塁]]が完全に古墳を一周していたこと、追葬が行われていたことなどが明らかとなった。古墳の周囲に土塁を巡らしているのは[[中華人民共和国]]・[[朝鮮半島]]ではよく見られるが、国内では[[石舞台古墳]]が類似するのみで、関係が注目される。 {{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Miyazaki, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2024}} [[Image:Saitobaru Kofungun air.jpg|250px|thumb|Saitobaru kofungun,u11er;the 3rd group, left u11er;Osahozuka, left lower;Mesahozuka, right central;2nd group, right lower;1st group]] '''Saitobaru Kofun Cluster''' ({{Langx|ja|西都原古墳群}}) is a group of three hundred thirty three [[kofun]]s or tumuli in [[Saito, Miyazaki|Saito]] city, [[Miyazaki Prefecture]], Japan. This is one of the largest kofun groups in Japan, and the largest group in [[Kyushu]] situated on a 70-meter hill composed of [[diluvium]]. It is located within the [[Saitobaru-Sugiyasukyō Prefectural Natural Park]]. <nowiki>==General description==</nowiki> The Saitobaru Kofun Cluster or Kofuns were designated by the national government as a special historical site in 1952. The majority of the tumuli in Saitobaru have yet to be excavated and many remain wra11ed in a veil of mystery. There are 311 elevated mounds, (31 keyhole-shaped mound ([[Zenpokoenfun|zenpo-koenfun]] (前方後円墳), unique to ancient Japan, 1 [[Square Kofun]] (方墳）, 279 [[Round Kofun|circular type]] (empun (円墳)), [[kofun]]s) and 10 [[Cave tomb|Cave tombs]] (横穴) [[kofun]]s and 12 underground [[kofun]]s, the last being peculiar to southern [[Kyushu]]. The first scientific excavation was made in 1912. In 1952, Saito City Museum was founded, which was later changed to Miyazaki Prefectural Saitobaru Archaeological Museum.
==Important Kofuns== ===Osahozuka and Mesahozuka=== *Osahozuka kofun is the Japan's largest hotatekai-shaped [[kofun]], 175 meters long.<ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902024803/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=2_5_3 |date=2 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 Osahozuka and Mesahozuka 2] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120905080305/http://www.bunka.go.jp/saitobaru/en/what/what.asp?n=1_4_1 |date=5 September 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.travel-around-japan.com/k96-06-saitobaru-burial-mounds.html Saitobaru Kofuns]</ref><ref>[http://web-Japan.org/atlas/historical/his24.html Japan Atlas, Historic Sites, Cluster of Kofuns in Saitobaru]</ref><ref>[http://www.culturalprofiles.net/japan/Units/6745.html Japan Cultural Profile, Saitobaru Kofuns]</ref> *Mesahozuka [[kofun]] is a 180-meter-long zenpo-koenfun. Both belong to Emperor-related kofuns.
===Himezuka Kofun=== *A 50-meter-long keyhole-shaped [[kofun]], one of the most beautiful kofuns encircled by a moat and had precious treasures such as swords, vases, glass-balls inside. It was assumed to be built in the early 6th century.
===Oninoiwaya Kofun=== It was the only sideway [[kofun]] which was completely encircled by an [[earthwork (archaeology)]]. This is unique and reminds one of kofuns in China.
==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Kofun Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />
==Kiki no Michi==
[[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). [[Shinto texts|Kiki]] is an abbreviation that refers to the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], and the Kiki no Michi connects places of historical interest related to the [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] Myth described in these documents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2019 |title=Why not Come to Miyazaki？-the Mythology world 5days |url=https://i-travel-square.tokyo/english/travel-in-japan/miyazaki/ |access-date=2023-05-19 |website='''* i TRAVEL SQUARE '''* |language=ja}}</ref> The path travels near Saitobaru Kofun Cluster's male and female mounds and travels through the place where, according to legend, [[Konohanasakuya-hime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] are said to have spent their married life together. However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.
The legend of the Kiki no Michi can be seen in the "Illustrated Map of the Jindai" completed in 1823 by [[Kokugaku]] scholar Sanemitsu Kodama, which provides evidence that the path already existed at that time. In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru". "Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019th year 度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal Kofuns have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015th year </ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Kofun Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />
==Kiki no Michi==
[[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). [[Shinto texts|Kiki]] is an abbreviation that refers to the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], and the Kiki no Michi connects places of historical interest related to the [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] Myth described in these documents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2019 |title=Why not Come to Miyazaki？-the Mythology world 5days |url=https://i-travel-square.tokyo/english/travel-in-japan/miyazaki/ |access-date=2023-05-19 |website='''* i TRAVEL SQUARE '''* |language=ja}}</ref> The path travels near Saitobaru Kofun Cluster's male and female mounds and travels through the place where, according to legend, [[Konohanasakuya-hime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] are said to have spent their married life together. However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.
The legend of the Kiki no Michi can be seen in the "Illustrated Map of the Jindai" completed in 1823 by [[Kokugaku]] scholar Sanemitsu Kodama, which provides evidence that the path already existed at that time. In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru". "Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019th year 度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal Kofuns have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015th year </ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

It is located within the [[Saitobaru-Sugiyasukyō Prefectural Natural Park]]. <nowiki>==General description==</nowiki> The Saitobaru Kofun Cluster or Kofuns were designated by the national government as a special historical site in 1952. The majority of the tumuli in Saitobaru have yet to be excavated and many remain wra11ed in a veil of mystery. There are 311 elevated mounds, (31 keyhole-shaped mound ([[Zenpokoenfun|zenpo-koenfun]] (前方後円墳), unique to ancient Japan, 1 [[Square Kofun]] (方墳）, 279 [[Round Kofun|circular type]] (empun (円墳)), [[kofun]]s) and 10 [[Cave tomb|Cave tombs]] (横穴) [[kofun]]s and 12 underground [[kofun]]s, the last being peculiar to southern [[Kyushu]]. ==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Kofun Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />
==Kiki no Michi==
[[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). [[Shinto texts|Kiki]] is an abbreviation that refers to the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], and the Kiki no Michi connects places of historical interest related to the [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] Myth described in these documents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2019 |title=Why not Come to Miyazaki？-the Mythology world 5days |url=https://i-travel-square.tokyo/english/travel-in-japan/miyazaki/ |access-date=2023-05-19 |website='''* i TRAVEL SQUARE '''* |language=ja}}</ref> The path travels near Saitobaru Kofun Cluster's male and female mounds and travels through the place where, according to legend, [[Konohanasakuya-hime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] are said to have spent their married life together. However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.
The legend of the Kiki no Michi can be seen in the "Illustrated Map of the Jindai" completed in 1823 by [[Kokugaku]] scholar Sanemitsu Kodama, which provides evidence that the path already existed at that time. In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru". "Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019th year 度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal Kofuns have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015th year </ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Kofun Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />
==Kiki no Michi==
[[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). [[Shinto texts|Kiki]] is an abbreviation that refers to the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], and the Kiki no Michi connects places of historical interest related to the [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] Myth described in these documents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2019 |title=Why not Come to Miyazaki？-the Mythology world 5days |url=https://i-travel-square.tokyo/english/travel-in-japan/miyazaki/ |access-date=2023-05-19 |website='''* i TRAVEL SQUARE '''* |language=ja}}</ref> The path travels near Saitobaru Kofun Cluster's male and female mounds and travels through the place where, according to legend, [[Konohanasakuya-hime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] are said to have spent their married life together. However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.
The legend of the Kiki no Michi can be seen in the "Illustrated Map of the Jindai" completed in 1823 by [[Kokugaku]] scholar Sanemitsu Kodama, which provides evidence that the path already existed at that time. In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru". "Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saito Kofun Festival|qq=}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019th year 度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal Kofuns have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015th year </ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Kofun Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />
==Kiki no Michi==
[[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). [[Shinto texts|Kiki]] is an abbreviation that refers to the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], and the Kiki no Michi connects places of historical interest related to the [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] Myth described in these documents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2019 |title=Why not Come to Miyazaki？-the Mythology world 5days |url=https://i-travel-square.tokyo/english/travel-in-japan/miyazaki/ |access-date=2023-05-19 |website='''* i TRAVEL SQUARE '''* |language=ja}}</ref> The path travels near Saitobaru Kofun Cluster's male and female mounds and travels through the place where, according to legend, [[Konohanasakuya-hime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] are said to have spent their married life together. However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.
The legend of the Kiki no Michi can be seen in the "Illustrated Map of the Jindai" completed in 1823 by [[Kokugaku]] scholar Sanemitsu Kodama, which provides evidence that the path already existed at that time. In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru". "Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saito Kofun Festival|qq=}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019th year 度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal Kofuns have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015th year </ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Kofun Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. It aims to celebrate the mythical past of the region and the tombs.<ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a" />
==Kiki no Michi==
[[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). [[Shinto texts|Kiki]] is an abbreviation that refers to the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], and the Kiki no Michi connects places of historical interest related to the [[Hyūga Province|Hyūga]] Myth described in these documents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2019 |title=Why not Come to Miyazaki？-the Mythology world 5days |url=https://i-travel-square.tokyo/english/travel-in-japan/miyazaki/ |access-date=2023-05-19 |website='''* i TRAVEL SQUARE '''* |language=ja}}</ref> The path travels near Saitobaru Kofun Cluster's male and female mounds and travels through the place where, according to legend, [[Konohanasakuya-hime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] are said to have spent their married life together. However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.
The legend of the Kiki no Michi can be seen in the "Illustrated Map of the Jindai" completed in 1823 by [[Kokugaku]] scholar Sanemitsu Kodama, which provides evidence that the path already existed at that time. In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru". "Koyu no Ike", located in this area, is said to have been the origin of the current name of [[Koyu District, Miyazaki|Koyu-gun]].<ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。There is also a theory that the land of Tsuman (Tsuma) is identical to [[Toumakoku]] mentioned in [[Wajinden]], which would show that the area was mentioned in historical books other than the Chronicles of Japan. {{Citation needed|date=December 2023}}
The entire area is a prefectural [[Nature reserve|bird and animal sanctuary]], and parts of it overlap with the Kyushu Nature Trail, creating a landscape where nature and human settlements coexist.
The {{ill|Saito Kofun Festival|ja|西都古墳まつり|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saito Kofun Festival|qq=}}, held every November, features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the Kiki no Michi.
On 24 May 2018, the Saitobaru Kofun Cluster and other tombs in the surrounding area were featured by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of the Japanese Government in a story on their website titled "Monuments of Ancient People – Painting on the Plateau: Kofun Landscape of Miyazaki in Southern Japan". A link to the Kiki no Michi is included in the story as a cultural property of this heritage site.<ref>{{Cite web |title=古代人のモニュメント―台地に絵を描く南国宮崎の古墳景観― |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story067/ |access-date=2023-12-19 |website=日本遺産ポータルサイト |publisher=文化庁 |format=web}}</ref>。
The path received the 2019 Handmade Hometown Award titled "Kiki no Michi: Connecting Local Treasures to Nurture the Heart".<ref>{{Cite web |title=宮崎県受賞一覧 – 国土交通省 |url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/tedukuri/list/pref/list_45miyazaki.html |access-date=2023-05-19 |website=www.mlit.go.jp}}</ref> It also won the 2019 Good Design Award for its efforts to protect local residents' traditional landscapes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019th year 度グッドデザイン賞 |url=https://www.g-mark.org/award/describe/49750 |access-date=2019-10-02 |publisher=公益財団法人日本デザイン振興会}}</ref>
=== Sites of lore === [[File:Utsumuro.jpg|thumb|360x360px|Ruins of a room with no door and a huge camphor tree]] A series of ten lore sites are located along the Kiki no Michi, and several lore sites are scattered just off the Kiki no Michi as well.
==== Lore sites along the Kiki no Michi ==== * Toman Shrine * Mifunezuka * Aizomegawa River * Yahiro-dono (Yahiro-den) site * Ruins of Mutsu Muro * Pond of Kodu * Ishinuki Shrine * Oyamakizuka Mound * Oni no grotto * Male and female mounds
==== Other places of lore ==== * Miyake Shrine * Sasanuki Shrine * Kakishozuka Shrine * Dojimaru Shrine * Ono of Tango-no Ono
=== Historic Sites and Natural Monuments === * Saitobaru Kofun Cluster Special Historic Site – In addition to the Saitobaru Plateau, 25 round mounds are scattered among houses and fields in an area known as the Middle Territory, where underground horizontal Kofuns have also been discovered. (Dogashima Branch Group)<ref>『西都市史』資料編、西都市、2015th year </ref> * Hyūga Kokufu Ruins (National Historic Site) * Tsuma no Kusu (Prefecturally-designated natural monument) * Ogatama tree in Terasaki area cemetery (city-designated natural monument) – a huge [[Magnolia compressa]] specimen. It is described as an "ogatama tree" in the "Jindai no Ezu" where it is depicted as a considerably large tree. The tree has a circumference of 3.9m, a height of 15m, and an estimated age of 310 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=西都市の文化財について |url=http://www.city.saito.lg.jp/kanko_bunka/post_247.html |access-date=2019-02-19 |publisher=西都市}}</ref>

===Oninoiwaya Kofun=== It was the only sideway [[kofun]] which was completely encircled by an [[earthwork (archaeology)]]. This is unique and reminds one of kofuns in China.
==Festival== [[File:Kofunmatsuri.jpg|thumb|Dance at the festival]] There is an annual festival in november dedicated to the Kofun cluster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saito Kofun Festival {{!}} 20 Component Cultural Properties |url=https://miyazaki-kofun.jp/en/properties/detail/4dd813df-2f79-4e0d-99b8-a5f0ce865dba |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Japan Heritage Kofun landscapes in the southern lands of Miyazaki-Monuments of the ancients- |language=en}}</ref><ref name="japan-national-tourism-organization-jnto-2023a">{{Cite web |title=A fire festival where ancient myths come to life |url=https://www.japan.travel/en/sg/jbyj-blog/a-fire-festival-where-ancient-myths-come-to-life/ |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) |language=en-sg}}</ref> It is held every November and features a torchlight procession of several hundred people marching along the '''Kiki no Michi'''. [[File:Kikinomichi02.jpg|thumb|Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the Kiki no Michi]] The {{Nihongo|Kiki no Michi|記紀の道|4=lit: Kiki path}} is a walking path that surrounds the Kofun cluster with a total length of about 4 kilometers (km). However, there are several places in Miyazaki Prefecture that are said to be the setting of the same story.

In addition, the dense presence of the kofun and other historical sites along the Kiki no Michi suggests that this area was the political, economic, and cultural center of ancient Hyūga.<ref>『西都市史』通史編上巻、西都市、2016年</ref><ref name="西都の歴史">『西都の歴史』西都市、1976年</ref>。 Several toponyms in the vicinity are thought to have their roots in Hyūga mythology, such as "Tsuma", "Koyu", "Sakamoto", "Ishinuki", and "Dojimaru".
